question: Under the definitions in the consolidated Prospectus for Germany of Guggenheim Global Investments plc dated 9 November 2023 (which consolidates the Company's prospectus dated 4 September 2023), could the Directors of Guggenheim Global Investments plc set up a Fund that has only one Dealing Day in a calendar month? Explain what a Dealing Day is and where the term 'Business Day' on which it is based is specified.
reference_answer: No. A 'Dealing Day' is defined, for each Fund, as each Business Day on which subscriptions for, redemptions of and exchanges of relevant Shares can be made by the Company, as specified in the Supplement for the relevant Fund and/or such other Dealing Days as the Directors determine and notify to Shareholders in advance, provided that there are at least two Dealing Days in each month occurring at regular intervals. 'Business Day' is not defined in the Prospectus itself: it means, in relation to any Fund, each day specified as such in the Supplement for the relevant Fund. So at least two Dealing Days per month, at regular intervals, are required.

evidence.text: "Business Day"                    means, in relation to any Fund, each day as is specified as such in the Supplement for the relevant Fund;

"Dealing Day"                   means, in respect of each Fund, each Business Day on which subscriptions for, redemptions of and exchanges of relevant Shares can be made by the Company as specified in the
advance, provided that there shall be at least two Dealing Days in each month occurring at regular intervals;

question: According to the fees and expenses section of the consolidated Prospectus for Germany of Guggenheim Global Investments plc dated 9 November 2023 (which consolidates the Company's prospectus dated 4 September 2023), which is higher: the maximum annual administration fee rate payable to the Administrator or the maximum annual fee rate payable to the Depositary (both expressed as a percentage of each Fund's Net Asset Value)? State both rates, the gap in percentage points, and the minimum annual administration fee in US dollars.
reference_answer: The Administrator's maximum fee, up to 0.05% per annum of each Fund's Net Asset Value (subject to a minimum fee of USD 50,000 per annum), is higher than the Depositary's maximum fee of up to 0.023% per annum of each Fund's Net Asset Value. The gap is 0.027 percentage points (0.05% - 0.023%), i.e. 2.7 basis points. The Depositary's fee is subject to a tiered arrangement under which actual fees fall as a Fund's NAV grows, and both are quoted exclusive of VAT.

evidence.text: fee accrued at each Dealing Day and payable monthly in arrears, of up to 0.05 per cent per annum of the Net Asset Value of each Fund subject to a minimum fee of $50,000 per annum.
fee accrued daily and payable monthly in arrears, of up to 0.023 per cent per annum of the Net Asset Value of each Fund.

question: What risk does the consolidated Prospectus for Germany of Guggenheim Global Investments plc dated 9 November 2023 (which consolidates the Company's prospectus dated 4 September 2023) describe for investors in other share classes when a Guggenheim Global Investments plc Fund hedges currency exposure at Class level, and what limits on over-hedged and under-hedged positions (as % of the relevant Class's Net Asset Value) does it say apply to such hedging?
reference_answer: Risk ('Currency Hedging at Class Level Risk'): hedging at Class level may expose the Fund to cross contamination risk, because it may not be possible to ensure that a counterparty's recourse is limited to the assets of the relevant Class. Although costs, gains and losses accrue solely to the relevant Class, hedging in one Class may impact negatively on another Class, particularly where EMIR or the DF Act require the Fund to post collateral (initial or variation margin); that collateral is posted at the Fund's risk, not the Class's, because the Class is not a segregated portion of the Fund's assets. Limits: over-hedged positions should not exceed 105% of the Net Asset Value of the relevant Class, and under-hedged positions should not fall short of 95% of the portion of the Class's Net Asset Value that is to be hedged against currency risk.

evidence.text: Currency Hedging at Class Level Risk: Hedging activity at Class level may expose the Fund to cross contamination risk as it may not be possible to ensure (contractually or otherwise) that a counterparty's recourse in any such arrangements is limited to the assets of the relevant Class.

Over-hedged positions should not exceed 105% of the Net Asset Value of the relevant Class; … Under-hedged positions should not fall short of 95% of the portion of the Net Asset Value of the relevant Class which is to be hedged against currency risk;

question: A sub-fund of Guggenheim Global Investments plc has net assets of USD 500 million and an OTC derivative counterparty exposure of USD 40 million to a single credit institution authorised in the United Kingdom. Ignoring any other exposure to that institution, does this comply with the OTC counterparty limit in the investment restrictions of the consolidated Prospectus for Germany of Guggenheim Global Investments plc dated 9 November 2023 (which consolidates the Company's prospectus dated 4 September 2023)? Give the applicable limit(s) as a percentage of net assets.
reference_answer: Yes. The exposure is 8% of net assets (USD 40 million / USD 500 million). The general limit for risk exposure to a counterparty to an OTC FDI is 5% of net assets, which would be exceeded, but it is raised to 10% where the counterparty is a 'Relevant Institution'. A Relevant Institution includes credit institutions authorised within a signatory state (other than an EEA Member State) to the Basle Capital Convergence Agreement of July 1988, which the Prospectus states includes the United Kingdom. So the 10% limit applies and 8% is within it.

evidence.text: The risk exposure of a Fund to a counterparty to an OTC FDI may not exceed 5 per cent of its net assets. This limit is raised to 10 per cent in the case of Relevant Institutions.

"Relevant Institution"    a credit institution authorised in an EEA Member State or credit institutions authorised within a signatory state (other than an EEA Member State) to the Basle Capital Convergence Agreement of July 1988 (which includes the United Kingdom)

question: Guggenheim Global Investments plc's Prospectus (consolidated Prospectus for Germany dated 9 November 2023, consolidating the prospectus of 4 September 2023) caps the aggregate Directors' remuneration at a stated annual amount. Were the Directors' fees charged for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 (excluding pension contributions), as reported in the Company's 2025 annual report and audited financial statements, within that cap? Give both amounts in euro and the headroom.
reference_answer: Yes. The Prospectus states that the aggregate amount of Directors' remuneration will not exceed EUR 114,000 per annum. The 2025 annual report states that Directors' fees charged for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 amounted to EUR 65 thousand (EUR 65,000; equivalent to USD 73 thousand), leaving EUR 49,000 of headroom below the cap (about 57% utilised). Directors' pension contributions to defined contribution schemes (EUR 49 thousand) are reported separately in the annual report and are not included in the EUR 65 thousand fees figure. Note the comparison is between a cap in a 2023 prospectus and 2025 actual fees.

evidence.text: The aggregate amount of Directors’ remuneration will not exceed €114,000 per annum.
Directors fees charged for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 amounted to USD‘000 73 (31 December 2024: USD‘000 70) (EUR'000 65, (31 December 2024: EUR'000 65))
